passages.text: Then the LORD said to Moses and Aaron, “When someone has a swelling or rash or bright spot on his skin that could become an infectious skin disease, he must be brought to Aaron the priest or to one of his sons who is a priest.
passages.sermon:
The LORD spoke to Moses and Aaron.
He gave them instructions.
A person may have a problem on his skin.
This problem could be a swelling, a rash, or a bright spot.
These signs may mean the person has a serious skin disease.
The person must go to Aaron the priest.
If Aaron is not available, the person must go to one of Aaron’s sons who is a priest.
passages.original: וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אֶל־ מֹשֶׁ֥ה וְאֶֽל־ אַהֲרֹ֖ן לֵאמֹֽר׃ אָדָ֗ם כִּֽי־ יִהְיֶ֤ה בְעוֹר־ בְּשָׂרוֹ֙ שְׂאֵ֤ת אֽוֹ־ סַפַּ֙חַת֙ א֣וֹ בַהֶ֔רֶת וְהָיָ֥ה בְעוֹר־ בְּשָׂר֖וֹ לְנֶ֣גַע צָרָ֑עַת וְהוּבָא֙ אֶל־ אַהֲרֹ֣ן הַכֹּהֵ֔ן א֛וֹ אֶל־ אַחַ֥ד מִבָּנָ֖יו הַכֹּהֲנִֽים׃

passages.text: The priest is to examine the infection on his skin, and if the hair in the infection has turned white and the sore appears to be deeper than the skin, it is a skin disease. After the priest examines him, he must pronounce him unclean.
passages.sermon:
A priest examines a person’s skin.
The priest looks at the infected area.
If the hair in the infection has turned white, the priest notices this.
If the sore looks deeper than the skin, the priest sees this.
This is a skin disease called tzaraat.
The priest examines the person.
The priest declares the person unclean.
passages.original: וְרָאָ֣ה הַכֹּהֵ֣ן אֶת־ הַנֶּ֣גַע בְּעֽוֹר־ הַ֠בָּשָׂר וְשֵׂעָ֨ר בַּנֶּ֜גַע הָפַ֣ךְ׀ לָבָ֗ן וּמַרְאֵ֤ה הַנֶּ֙גַע֙ עָמֹק֙ מֵע֣וֹר בְּשָׂר֔וֹ נֶ֥גַע צָרַ֖עַת ה֑וּא וְרָאָ֥הוּ הַכֹּהֵ֖ן וְטִמֵּ֥א אֹתֽוֹ׃

passages.text: If, however, the spot on his skin is white and does not appear to be deeper than the skin, and the hair in it has not turned white, the priest shall isolate the infected person for seven days.
passages.sermon:
A person may have a white spot on the skin of his body.
The spot does not look deeper than the skin.
The hair in the spot has not turned white.
The priest must see the spot.
The priest must separate the person with the spot.
The priest must keep him apart for seven days.
passages.original: וְאִם־ בַּהֶרֶת֩ לְבָנָ֨ה הִ֜וא בְּע֣וֹר בְּשָׂר֗וֹ וְעָמֹק֙ אֵין־ מַרְאֶ֣הָ מִן־ הָע֔וֹר וּשְׂעָרָ֖ה לֹא־ הָפַ֣ךְ לָבָ֑ן וְהִסְגִּ֧יר הַכֹּהֵ֛ן אֶת־ הַנֶּ֖גַע שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִֽים׃

passages.text: On the seventh day the priest is to reexamine him, and if he sees that the infection is unchanged and has not spread on the skin, the priest must isolate him for another seven days.
passages.sermon:
A priest examines a person with a skin infection.
The priest examines the person on the seventh day.
The priest looks at the infection.
The infection has not changed.
The infection has not spread on the skin.
The priest isolates the person for another seven days.
passages.original: וְרָאָ֣הוּ הַכֹּהֵן֮ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי֒ וְהִנֵּ֤ה הַנֶּ֙גַע֙ עָמַ֣ד בְּעֵינָ֔יו לֹֽא־ פָשָׂ֥ה הַנֶּ֖גַע בָּע֑וֹר וְהִסְגִּיר֧וֹ הַכֹּהֵ֛ן שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֖ים שֵׁנִֽית׃

passages.text: The priest will examine him again on the seventh day, and if the sore has faded and has not spread on the skin, the priest shall pronounce him clean; it is a rash. The person must wash his clothes and be clean.
passages.sermon:
A priest examines a person with a skin disease.
The priest examines him again on the seventh day.
The priest sees that the sore has faded.
The priest sees that the sore has not spread on the skin.
The priest pronounces the person clean.
The priest says it is only a rash.
The person must wash his clothes.
The person becomes clean.
passages.original: וְרָאָה֩ הַכֹּהֵ֨ן אֹת֜וֹ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי֮ שֵׁנִית֒ וְהִנֵּה֙ כֵּהָ֣ה הַנֶּ֔גַע וְלֹא־ פָשָׂ֥ה הַנֶּ֖גַע בָּע֑וֹר וְטִהֲר֤וֹ הַכֹּהֵן֙ מִסְפַּ֣חַת הִ֔יא וְכִבֶּ֥ס בְּגָדָ֖יו וְטָהֵֽר׃

passages.text: But if the rash spreads further on his skin after he has shown himself to the priest for his cleansing, he must present himself again to the priest.
passages.sermon:
A person may have a rash on his skin.
He must go to the priest for examination and cleansing.
If the rash spreads further on his skin after this,
He must go again to the priest.
The priest will examine him again.
passages.original: וְאִם־ פָּשֹׂ֨ה תִפְשֶׂ֤ה הַמִּסְפַּ֙חַת֙ בָּע֔וֹר אַחֲרֵ֧י הֵרָאֹת֛וֹ אֶל־ הַכֹּהֵ֖ן לְטָהֳרָת֑וֹ וְנִרְאָ֥ה שֵׁנִ֖ית אֶל־ הַכֹּהֵֽן׃

passages.text: The priest will reexamine him, and if the rash has spread on the skin, the priest must pronounce him unclean; he has a skin disease.
passages.sermon:
A priest examines a person with a skin rash.
The priest looks to see if the rash has spread on the skin.
If the rash has spread, the priest declares the person unclean.
The person has a skin disease.
passages.original: וְרָאָה֙ הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וְהִנֵּ֛ה פָּשְׂתָ֥ה הַמִּסְפַּ֖חַת בָּע֑וֹר וְטִמְּא֥וֹ הַכֹּהֵ֖ן צָרַ֥עַת הִֽוא׃פ

passages.text: When anyone develops a skin disease, he must be brought to the priest.
passages.sermon:
A person may develop a skin disease.
This disease is called tzaraat.
The person must go to the priest.
passages.original: נֶ֣גַע צָרַ֔עַת כִּ֥י תִהְיֶ֖ה בְּאָדָ֑ם וְהוּבָ֖א אֶל־ הַכֹּהֵֽן׃

passages.text: The priest will examine him, and if there is a white swelling on the skin that has turned the hair white, and there is raw flesh in the swelling, it is a chronic skin disease and the priest must pronounce him unclean. He need not isolate him, for he is unclean.
passages.sermon:
A priest examines a person with a skin disease.
He looks for a white swelling on the skin.
He checks if the hair in the swelling has turned white.
He looks for raw flesh inside the swelling.
If the swelling is white, the hair is white, and there is raw flesh, the person has a chronic skin disease.
The priest must declare the person unclean.
The priest does not need to isolate the person.
The person is already unclean.
passages.original: וְרָאָ֣ה הַכֹּהֵ֗ן וְהִנֵּ֤ה שְׂאֵת־ לְבָנָה֙ בָּע֔וֹר וְהִ֕יא הָפְכָ֖ה שֵׂעָ֣ר לָבָ֑ן וּמִֽחְיַ֛ת בָּשָׂ֥ר חַ֖י בַּשְׂאֵֽת׃ צָרַ֨עַת נוֹשֶׁ֤נֶת הִוא֙ בְּע֣וֹר בְּשָׂר֔וֹ וְטִמְּא֖וֹ הַכֹּהֵ֑ן לֹ֣א יַסְגִּרֶ֔נּוּ כִּ֥י טָמֵ֖א הֽוּא׃

passages.text: But if the skin disease breaks out all over his skin so that it covers all the skin of the infected person from head to foot, as far as the priest can see, the priest shall examine him, and if the disease has covered his entire body, he is to pronounce the infected person clean. Since it has all turned white, he is clean.
passages.sermon:
A person may develop a skin disease.
This disease can spread over the skin.
It may cover all the skin of the infected person.
It can go from the head to the feet.
The priest must look at the person.
The priest checks if the disease covers the whole body.
If the disease covers all the skin, the priest must decide.
If the skin has all turned white, the priest pronounces the person clean.
The person is clean because the skin is completely white.
passages.original: וְאִם־ פָּר֨וֹחַ תִּפְרַ֤ח הַצָּרַ֙עַת֙ בָּע֔וֹר וְכִסְּתָ֣ה הַצָּרַ֗עַת אֵ֚ת כָּל־ ע֣וֹר הַנֶּ֔גַע מֵרֹאשׁ֖וֹ וְעַד־ רַגְלָ֑יו לְכָל־ מַרְאֵ֖ה עֵינֵ֥י הַכֹּהֵֽן׃ וְרָאָ֣ה הַכֹּהֵ֗ן וְהִנֵּ֨ה כִסְּתָ֤ה הַצָּרַ֙עַת֙ אֶת־ כָּל־ בְּשָׂר֔וֹ וְטִהַ֖ר אֶת־ הַנָּ֑גַע כֻּלּ֛וֹ הָפַ֥ךְ לָבָ֖ן טָה֥וֹר הֽוּא׃

passages.text: But whenever raw flesh appears on someone, he will be unclean.
passages.sermon: Raw flesh can appear on a person’s skin.\r\nThis raw flesh means the person is unclean.
passages.original: וּבְי֨וֹם הֵרָא֥וֹת בּ֛וֹ בָּשָׂ֥ר חַ֖י יִטְמָֽא׃

passages.text: When the priest sees the raw flesh, he must pronounce him unclean. The raw flesh is unclean; it is a skin disease.
passages.sermon:
The priest examines the person.
The priest sees raw flesh on the skin.
The priest declares the person unclean.
Raw flesh is unclean.
Raw flesh means there is a skin disease.
passages.original: וְרָאָ֧ה הַכֹּהֵ֛ן אֶת־ הַבָּשָׂ֥ר הַחַ֖י וְטִמְּא֑וֹ הַבָּשָׂ֥ר הַחַ֛י טָמֵ֥א ה֖וּא צָרַ֥עַת הֽוּא׃

passages.text: But if the raw flesh changes and turns white, he must go to the priest.
passages.sermon:
A person may have raw flesh on his skin.
The raw flesh may change.
The raw flesh may turn white.
If the raw flesh turns white, the person must go to the priest.
passages.original: א֣וֹ כִ֥י יָשׁ֛וּב הַבָּשָׂ֥ר הַחַ֖י וְנֶהְפַּ֣ךְ לְלָבָ֑ן וּבָ֖א אֶל־ הַכֹּהֵֽן׃

passages.text: The priest will reexamine him, and if the infection has turned white, the priest is to pronounce the infected person clean; then he is clean.
passages.sermon:
A priest examines a person with a skin infection.
The priest looks at the infected area.
If the infection has turned white, the priest makes a decision.
The priest pronounces the person clean.
The person is now clean.
passages.original: וְרָאָ֙הוּ֙ הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וְהִנֵּ֛ה נֶהְפַּ֥ךְ הַנֶּ֖גַע לְלָבָ֑ן וְטִהַ֧ר הַכֹּהֵ֛ן אֶת־ הַנֶּ֖גַע טָה֥וֹר הֽוּא׃פ

passages.text: When a boil appears on someone’s skin and it heals, and a white swelling or a reddish-white spot develops where the boil was, he must present himself to the priest.
passages.sermon:
A person may have a boil on his skin.
The boil heals.
A white swelling may appear where the boil was.
A reddish-white spot may also appear where the boil was.
The person must go to the priest.
passages.original: וּבָשָׂ֕ר כִּֽי־ יִהְיֶ֥ה בֽוֹ־ בְעֹר֖וֹ שְׁחִ֑ין וְנִרְפָּֽא׃ וְהָיָ֞ה בִּמְק֤וֹם הַשְּׁחִין֙ שְׂאֵ֣ת לְבָנָ֔ה א֥וֹ בַהֶ֖רֶת לְבָנָ֣ה אֲדַמְדָּ֑מֶת וְנִרְאָ֖ה אֶל־ הַכֹּהֵֽן׃

passages.text: The priest shall examine it, and if it appears to be beneath the skin and the hair in it has turned white, the priest shall pronounce him unclean; it is a diseased infection that has broken out in the boil.
passages.sermon:
A priest examines the spot on the skin.
The spot looks lower than the rest of the skin.
The hair in the spot has turned white.
The priest declares the person unclean.
This is a diseased infection.
The infection has come out from the boil.
passages.original: וְרָאָ֣ה הַכֹּהֵ֗ן וְהִנֵּ֤ה מַרְאֶ֙הָ֙ שָׁפָ֣ל מִן־ הָע֔וֹר וּשְׂעָרָ֖הּ הָפַ֣ךְ לָבָ֑ן וְטִמְּא֧וֹ הַכֹּהֵ֛ן נֶֽגַע־ צָרַ֥עַת הִ֖וא בַּשְּׁחִ֥ין פָּרָֽחָה׃

passages.text: But when the priest examines it, if there is no white hair in it, and it is not beneath the skin and has faded, the priest shall isolate him for seven days.
passages.sermon:
A priest examines a skin spot on a person.
The spot does not have any white hair in it.
The spot is not deeper than the skin.
The spot has faded in color.
The priest must isolate the person for seven days.
passages.original: וְאִ֣ם׀ יִרְאֶ֣נָּה הַכֹּהֵ֗ן וְהִנֵּ֤ה אֵֽין־ בָּהּ֙ שֵׂעָ֣ר לָבָ֔ן וּשְׁפָלָ֥ה אֵינֶ֛נָּה מִן־ הָע֖וֹר וְהִ֣יא כֵהָ֑ה וְהִסְגִּיר֥וֹ הַכֹּהֵ֖ן שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִֽים׃

passages.text: If it spreads any further on the skin, the priest must pronounce him unclean; it is an infection.
passages.sermon:
A priest examines a person’s skin.
If the infection spreads on the skin, the priest acts.
The priest declares the person unclean.
This spreading spot is an infection.
passages.original: וְאִם־ פָּשֹׂ֥ה תִפְשֶׂ֖ה בָּע֑וֹר וְטִמֵּ֧א הַכֹּהֵ֛ן אֹת֖וֹ נֶ֥גַע הִֽוא׃

passages.text: But if the spot remains unchanged and does not spread, it is only the scar from the boil, and the priest shall pronounce him clean.
passages.sermon:
A priest examines a person’s skin.
He sees a spot on the skin.
The spot does not change.
The spot does not spread.
This spot is only a scar from a boil.
The priest pronounces the person clean.
passages.original: וְאִם־ תַּחְתֶּ֜יהָ תַּעֲמֹ֤ד הַבַּהֶ֙רֶת֙ לֹ֣א פָשָׂ֔תָה צָרֶ֥בֶת הַשְּׁחִ֖ין הִ֑וא וְטִהֲר֖וֹ הַכֹּהֵֽן׃ס

passages.text: When there is a burn on someone’s skin and the raw area of the burn becomes reddish-white or white, the priest must examine it. If the hair in the spot has turned white and the spot appears to be deeper than the skin, it is a disease that has broken out in the burn. The priest must pronounce him unclean; it is a diseased infection.
passages.sermon:
A person may have a burn on their skin.
The burn may heal and leave a raw area.
This raw area may become reddish-white or white.
The priest must examine this spot.
If the hair in the spot has turned white, this is important.
If the spot looks deeper than the rest of the skin, this is also important.
This means a disease has appeared in the burn.
The priest must declare the person unclean.
This is a diseased infection.
passages.original: א֣וֹ בָשָׂ֔ר כִּֽי־ יִהְיֶ֥ה בְעֹר֖וֹ מִכְוַת־ אֵ֑שׁ וְֽהָיְתָ֞ה מִֽחְיַ֣ת הַמִּכְוָ֗ה בַּהֶ֛רֶת לְבָנָ֥ה אֲדַמְדֶּ֖מֶת א֥וֹ לְבָנָֽה׃ וְרָאָ֣ה אֹתָ֣הּ הַכֹּהֵ֡ן וְהִנֵּ֣ה נֶהְפַּךְ֩ שֵׂעָ֨ר לָבָ֜ן בַּבַּהֶ֗רֶת וּמַרְאֶ֙הָ֙ עָמֹ֣ק מִן־ הָע֔וֹר צָרַ֣עַת הִ֔וא בַּמִּכְוָ֖ה פָּרָ֑חָה וְטִמֵּ֤א אֹתוֹ֙ הַכֹּהֵ֔ן נֶ֥גַע צָרַ֖עַת הִֽוא׃

passages.text: But if the priest examines it and there is no white hair in the spot, and it is not beneath the skin but has faded, the priest shall isolate him for seven days.
passages.sermon:
A priest examines a skin spot on a person.
The spot does not have white hair in it.
The spot is not deeper than the skin.
The spot looks faded.
The priest must isolate the person for seven days.
passages.original: וְאִ֣ם׀ יִרְאֶ֣נָּה הַכֹּהֵ֗ן וְהִנֵּ֤ה אֵֽין־ בַּבֶּהֶ֙רֶת֙ שֵׂעָ֣ר לָבָ֔ן וּשְׁפָלָ֥ה אֵינֶ֛נָּה מִן־ הָע֖וֹר וְהִ֣וא כֵהָ֑ה וְהִסְגִּיר֥וֹ הַכֹּהֵ֖ן שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִֽים׃

passages.text: On the seventh day the priest is to reexamine him, and if it has spread further on the skin, the priest must pronounce him unclean; it is a diseased infection.
passages.sermon:
A priest examines a person on the seventh day.
The priest looks at the skin.
If the infection has spread on the skin, the priest acts.
The priest must declare the person unclean.
This is a diseased infection.
passages.original: וְרָאָ֥הוּ הַכֹּהֵ֖ן בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֑י אִם־ פָּשֹׂ֤ה תִפְשֶׂה֙ בָּע֔וֹר וְטִמֵּ֤א הַכֹּהֵן֙ אֹת֔וֹ נֶ֥גַע צָרַ֖עַת הִֽוא׃

passages.text: But if the spot is unchanged and has not spread on the skin but has faded, it is a swelling from the burn, and the priest is to pronounce him clean; for it is only the scar from the burn.
passages.sermon:
A priest examines a person who has a spot on the skin from a burn.
If the spot does not change and does not spread on the skin, the priest observes this.
If the spot has faded, the priest notes this.
This spot is a swelling from the burn.
The priest pronounces the person clean.
It is only a scar from the burn.
passages.original: וְאִם־ תַּחְתֶּיהָ֩ תַעֲמֹ֨ד הַבַּהֶ֜רֶת לֹא־ פָשְׂתָ֤ה בָעוֹר֙ וְהִ֣וא כֵהָ֔ה שְׂאֵ֥ת הַמִּכְוָ֖ה הִ֑וא וְטִֽהֲרוֹ֙ הַכֹּהֵ֔ן כִּֽי־ צָרֶ֥בֶת הַמִּכְוָ֖ה הִֽוא׃פ

passages.text: If a man or woman has an infection on the head or chin, the priest shall examine the infection, and if it appears to be deeper than the skin and the hair in it is yellow and thin, the priest must pronounce him unclean; it is a scaly outbreak, an infectious disease of the head or chin.
passages.sermon:
A man or a woman may have an infection on the head or chin.
The priest examines the infection.
The infection may look deeper than the skin.
The hair in the infection may be yellow and thin.
The priest must pronounce the person unclean.
This is a scaly outbreak.
This is an infectious disease of the head or chin.
passages.original: וְאִישׁ֙ א֣וֹ אִשָּׁ֔ה כִּֽי־ יִהְיֶ֥ה ב֖וֹ נָ֑גַע בְּרֹ֖אשׁ א֥וֹ בְזָקָֽן׃ וְרָאָ֨ה הַכֹּהֵ֜ן אֶת־ הַנֶּ֗גַע וְהִנֵּ֤ה מַרְאֵ֙הוּ֙ עָמֹ֣ק מִן־ הָע֔וֹר וּב֛וֹ שֵׂעָ֥ר צָהֹ֖ב דָּ֑ק וְטִמֵּ֨א אֹת֤וֹ הַכֹּהֵן֙ נֶ֣תֶק ה֔וּא צָרַ֧עַת הָרֹ֛אשׁ א֥וֹ הַזָּקָ֖ן הֽוּא׃

passages.text: But if the priest examines the scaly infection and it does not appear to be deeper than the skin, and there is no black hair in it, the priest shall isolate the infected person for seven days.
passages.sermon:
A priest examines a person with a scaly infection.
The infection does not look deeper than the skin.
There is no black hair in the infection.
The priest isolates the person with the infection for seven days.
passages.original: וְכִֽי־ יִרְאֶ֨ה הַכֹּהֵ֜ן אֶת־ נֶ֣גַע הַנֶּ֗תֶק וְהִנֵּ֤ה אֵין־ מַרְאֵ֙הוּ֙ עָמֹ֣ק מִן־ הָע֔וֹר וְשֵׂעָ֥ר שָׁחֹ֖ר אֵ֣ין בּ֑וֹ וְהִסְגִּ֧יר הַכֹּהֵ֛ן אֶת־ נֶ֥גַע הַנֶּ֖תֶק שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִֽים׃

passages.text: On the seventh day the priest is to reexamine the infection, and if the scaly outbreak has not spread and there is no yellow hair in it, and it does not appear to be deeper than the skin, then the person must shave himself except for the scaly area. Then the priest shall isolate him for another seven days.
passages.sermon:
A priest examines a person with a scaly infection on the head or chin.
He examines the infection on the seventh day.
If the scaly outbreak has not spread, the priest observes this.
If there is no yellow hair in the infected area, the priest notes this.
If the infection does not look deeper than the skin, the priest sees this.
The person must shave himself.
He must not shave the area with the scaly infection.
The priest isolates the person for another seven days.
passages.original: וְרָאָ֨ה הַכֹּהֵ֣ן אֶת־ הַנֶּגַע֮ בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי֒ וְהִנֵּה֙ לֹא־ פָשָׂ֣ה הַנֶּ֔תֶק וְלֹא־ הָ֥יָה ב֖וֹ שֵׂעָ֣ר צָהֹ֑ב וּמַרְאֵ֣ה הַנֶּ֔תֶק אֵ֥ין עָמֹ֖ק מִן־ הָעֽוֹר׃ וְהִ֨תְגַּלָּ֔ח וְאֶת־ הַנֶּ֖תֶק לֹ֣א יְגַלֵּ֑חַ וְהִסְגִּ֨יר הַכֹּהֵ֧ן אֶת־ הַנֶּ֛תֶק שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֖ים שֵׁנִֽית׃

passages.text: On the seventh day the priest shall examine the scaly outbreak, and if it has not spread on the skin and does not appear to be deeper than the skin, the priest is to pronounce him clean. He must wash his clothes, and he will be clean.
passages.sermon:
A priest examines a person with a scaly outbreak.
He does this on the seventh day.
The priest looks at the outbreak on the skin.
The outbreak has not spread on the skin.
The outbreak does not look deeper than the skin.
The priest pronounces the person clean.
The person must wash his clothes.
The person will be clean.
passages.original: וְרָאָה֩ הַכֹּהֵ֨ן אֶת־ הַנֶּ֜תֶק בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֗י וְ֠הִנֵּה לֹא־ פָשָׂ֤ה הַנֶּ֙תֶק֙ בָּע֔וֹר וּמַרְאֵ֕הוּ אֵינֶ֥נּוּ עָמֹ֖ק מִן־ הָע֑וֹר וְטִהַ֤ר אֹתוֹ֙ הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וְכִבֶּ֥ס בְּגָדָ֖יו וְטָהֵֽר׃

passages.text: If, however, the scaly outbreak spreads further on the skin after his cleansing, the priest is to examine him, and if the scaly outbreak has spread on the skin, the priest need not look for yellow hair; the person is unclean.
passages.sermon:
A priest examines a person who had a scaly outbreak on the skin.
The person was already declared clean before.
If the scaly outbreak spreads again on the skin after cleansing, the priest must look at him.
If the priest sees that the scaly outbreak has spread on the skin, the priest does not need to check for yellow hair.
The person is unclean.
passages.original: וְאִם־ פָּשֹׂ֥ה יִפְשֶׂ֛ה הַנֶּ֖תֶק בָּע֑וֹר אַחֲרֵ֖י טָהֳרָתֽוֹ׃ וְרָאָ֙הוּ֙ הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וְהִנֵּ֛ה פָּשָׂ֥ה הַנֶּ֖תֶק בָּע֑וֹר לֹֽא־ יְבַקֵּ֧ר הַכֹּהֵ֛ן לַשֵּׂעָ֥ר הַצָּהֹ֖ב טָמֵ֥א הֽוּא׃

passages.text: If, however, in his sight the scaly outbreak is unchanged and black hair has grown in it, then it has healed. He is clean, and the priest is to pronounce him clean.
passages.sermon:
A priest examines a person with a scaly outbreak on the skin.
The priest looks closely at the spot.
The priest sees that the outbreak has not changed.
The priest sees that black hair has grown in the spot.
The outbreak has healed.
The person is clean.
The priest pronounces the person clean.
passages.original: וְאִם־ בְּעֵינָיו֩ עָמַ֨ד הַנֶּ֜תֶק וְשֵׂעָ֨ר שָׁחֹ֧ר צָֽמַח־ בּ֛וֹ נִרְפָּ֥א הַנֶּ֖תֶק טָה֣וֹר ה֑וּא וְטִהֲר֖וֹ הַכֹּהֵֽן׃ס

passages.text: When a man or a woman has white spots on the skin, the priest shall examine them, and if the spots are dull white, it is a harmless rash that has broken out on the skin; the person is clean.
passages.sermon:
A man or a woman may have white spots on their skin.
The priest must examine these spots.
If the spots on the skin are dull white, this is a harmless rash.
The rash has broken out on the skin.
The person is clean.
passages.original: וְאִישׁ֙ אֽוֹ־ אִשָּׁ֔ה כִּֽי־ יִהְיֶ֥ה בְעוֹר־ בְּשָׂרָ֖ם בֶּהָרֹ֑ת בֶּהָרֹ֖ת לְבָנֹֽת׃ וְרָאָ֣ה הַכֹּהֵ֗ן וְהִנֵּ֧ה בְעוֹר־ בְּשָׂרָ֛ם בֶּהָרֹ֖ת כֵּה֣וֹת לְבָנֹ֑ת בֹּ֥הַק ה֛וּא פָּרַ֥ח בָּע֖וֹר טָה֥וֹר הֽוּא׃ס

passages.text: Now if a man loses his hair and is bald, he is still clean.
passages.sermon: A man may lose his hair.\r\nHe may become bald.\r\nHe is still clean.
passages.original: וְאִ֕ישׁ כִּ֥י יִמָּרֵ֖ט רֹאשׁ֑וֹ קֵרֵ֥חַ ה֖וּא טָה֥וֹר הֽוּא׃

passages.text: Or if his hairline recedes and he is bald on his forehead, he is still clean.
passages.sermon:
A man may lose hair from the front of his head.
His hairline may recede.
He may become bald on his forehead.
This man is still clean.
passages.original: וְאִם֙ מִפְּאַ֣ת פָּנָ֔יו יִמָּרֵ֖ט רֹאשׁ֑וֹ גִּבֵּ֥חַ ה֖וּא טָה֥וֹר הֽוּא׃

passages.text: But if there is a reddish-white sore on the bald head or forehead, it is an infectious disease breaking out on it.
passages.sermon:
A man may have a bald head or a bald forehead.
A sore may appear on his bald head or on his bald forehead.
The sore may be reddish-white.
This sore is an infectious disease.
The disease breaks out on his bald head or on his bald forehead.
passages.original: וְכִֽי־ יִהְיֶ֤ה בַקָּרַ֙חַת֙ א֣וֹ בַגַּבַּ֔חַת נֶ֖גַע לָבָ֣ן אֲדַמְדָּ֑ם צָרַ֤עַת פֹּרַ֙חַת֙ הִ֔וא בְּקָרַחְתּ֖וֹ א֥וֹ בְגַבַּחְתּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: The priest is to examine him, and if the swelling of the infection on his bald head or forehead is reddish-white like a skin disease, the man is diseased; he is unclean. The priest must pronounce him unclean because of the infection on his head.
passages.sermon:
A priest examines the man.
The man has a bald head or a bald forehead.
There is a swelling on his bald head or forehead.
The swelling is reddish-white.
The swelling looks like a skin disease.
The man has a disease.
The man is unclean.
The priest must declare the man unclean.
The infection is on the man’s head.
passages.original: וְרָאָ֨ה אֹת֜וֹ הַכֹּהֵ֗ן וְהִנֵּ֤ה שְׂאֵת־ הַנֶּ֙גַע֙ לְבָנָ֣ה אֲדַמְדֶּ֔מֶת בְּקָרַחְתּ֖וֹ א֣וֹ בְגַבַּחְתּ֑וֹ כְּמַרְאֵ֥ה צָרַ֖עַת ע֥וֹר בָּשָֽׂר׃ אִישׁ־ צָר֥וּעַ ה֖וּא טָמֵ֣א ה֑וּא טַמֵּ֧א יְטַמְּאֶ֛נּוּ הַכֹּהֵ֖ן בְּרֹאשׁ֥וֹ נִגְעֽוֹ׃

passages.text: A diseased person must wear torn clothes and let his hair hang loose, and he must cover his mouth and cry out, ‘Unclean, unclean!’
passages.sermon:
A person with a skin disease must follow special rules.
He must wear torn clothes.
He must let his hair hang loose.
He must cover his mouth.
He must call out, “Unclean, unclean!”
passages.original: וְהַצָּר֜וּעַ אֲשֶׁר־ בּ֣וֹ הַנֶּ֗גַע בְּגָדָ֞יו יִהְי֤וּ פְרֻמִים֙ וְרֹאשׁוֹ֙ יִהְיֶ֣ה פָר֔וּעַ וְעַל־ שָׂפָ֖ם יַעְטֶ֑ה וְטָמֵ֥א׀ טָמֵ֖א יִקְרָֽא׃

passages.text: As long as he has the infection, he remains unclean. He must live alone in a place outside the camp.
passages.sermon:
A man with a skin disease is unclean.
He stays unclean as long as the disease remains.
He must live by himself.
He must stay outside the camp.
passages.original: כָּל־ יְמֵ֞י אֲשֶׁ֨ר הַנֶּ֥גַע בּ֛וֹ יִטְמָ֖א טָמֵ֣א ה֑וּא בָּדָ֣ד יֵשֵׁ֔ב מִח֥וּץ לַֽמַּחֲנֶ֖ה מוֹשָׁבֽוֹ׃ס

passages.text: If any fabric is contaminated with mildew —any wool or linen garment, any weave or knit of linen or wool, or any article of leather— and if the mark in the fabric, leather, weave, knit, or leather article is green or red, then it is contaminated with mildew and must be shown to the priest.
passages.sermon:
A fabric can become contaminated with mildew.
This can happen to a wool garment.
This can happen to a linen garment.
This can happen to any woven or knitted item of linen or wool.
This can happen to any article made of leather.
The mildew may appear as a green mark.
The mildew may appear as a red mark.
The mark can be in the fabric.
The mark can be in the leather.
The mark can be in the weave or knit.
The mark can be in any leather article.
This is a mildew contamination.
The person must show the contaminated item to the priest.
passages.original: וְהַבֶּ֕גֶד כִּֽי־ יִהְיֶ֥ה ב֖וֹ נֶ֣גַע צָרָ֑עַת בְּבֶ֣גֶד צֶ֔מֶר א֖וֹ בְּבֶ֥גֶד פִּשְׁתִּֽים׃ א֤וֹ בִֽשְׁתִי֙ א֣וֹ בְעֵ֔רֶב לַפִּשְׁתִּ֖ים וְלַצָּ֑מֶר א֣וֹ בְע֔וֹר א֖וֹ בְּכָל־ מְלֶ֥אכֶת עֽוֹר׃ וְהָיָ֨ה הַנֶּ֜גַע יְרַקְרַ֣ק׀ א֣וֹ אֲדַמְדָּ֗ם בַּבֶּגֶד֩ א֨וֹ בָע֜וֹר אֽוֹ־ בַשְּׁתִ֤י אוֹ־ בָעֵ֙רֶב֙ א֣וֹ בְכָל־ כְּלִי־ ע֔וֹר נֶ֥גַע צָרַ֖עַת ה֑וּא וְהָרְאָ֖ה אֶת־ הַכֹּהֵֽן׃

passages.text: And the priest is to examine the mildew and isolate the contaminated fabric for seven days.
passages.sermon:
A priest examines the mildew.
The mildew is on a fabric.
The priest isolates the contaminated fabric.
He keeps it separate for seven days.
passages.original: וְרָאָ֥ה הַכֹּהֵ֖ן אֶת־ הַנָּ֑גַע וְהִסְגִּ֥יר אֶת־ הַנֶּ֖גַע שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִֽים׃

passages.text: On the seventh day the priest shall reexamine it, and if the mildew has spread in the fabric, weave, knit, or leather, then regardless of how it is used, it is a harmful mildew; the article is unclean.
passages.sermon:
A priest examines the contaminated item on the seventh day.
The item may be fabric, weave, knit, or leather.
The priest looks for mildew.
If the mildew has spread in the item, the priest makes a decision.
It does not matter how the leather is used.
If the mildew has spread, it is a harmful mildew.
The item is unclean.
passages.original: וְרָאָ֨ה אֶת־ הַנֶּ֜גַע בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִ֗י כִּֽי־ פָשָׂ֤ה הַנֶּ֙גַע֙ בַּ֠בֶּגֶד אֽוֹ־ בַשְּׁתִ֤י אֽוֹ־ בָעֵ֙רֶב֙ א֣וֹ בָע֔וֹר לְכֹ֛ל אֲשֶׁר־ יֵעָשֶׂ֥ה הָע֖וֹר לִמְלָאכָ֑ה צָרַ֧עַת מַמְאֶ֛רֶת הַנֶּ֖גַע טָמֵ֥א הֽוּא׃

passages.text: He is to burn the fabric, weave, or knit, whether the contaminated item is wool or linen or leather. Since the mildew is harmful, the article must be burned up.
passages.sermon:
The priest examines the item.
The item may be fabric, weave, knit, or leather.
The item may be made of wool or linen.
If the item has mildew, the priest must burn it.
The mildew is harmful.
The item must be burned in fire.
passages.original: וְשָׂרַ֨ף אֶת־ הַבֶּ֜גֶד א֥וֹ אֶֽת־ הַשְּׁתִ֣י׀ א֣וֹ אֶת־ הָעֵ֗רֶב בַּצֶּ֙מֶר֙ א֣וֹ בַפִּשְׁתִּ֔ים א֚וֹ אֶת־ כָּל־ כְּלִ֣י הָע֔וֹר אֲשֶׁר־ יִהְיֶ֥ה ב֖וֹ הַנָּ֑גַע כִּֽי־ צָרַ֤עַת מַמְאֶ֙רֶת֙ הִ֔וא בָּאֵ֖שׁ תִּשָּׂרֵֽף׃

passages.text: But when the priest reexamines it, if the mildew has not spread in the fabric, weave, knit, or leather article, the priest is to order the contaminated article to be washed and isolated for another seven days.
passages.sermon:
A priest examines the item.
The item may be fabric, weave, knit, or leather.
The priest looks for mildew on the item.
If the mildew has not spread, the priest gives instructions.
The priest orders the item with mildew to be washed.
After washing, the priest orders the item to be isolated.
The isolation lasts for another seven days.
passages.original: וְאִם֮ יִרְאֶ֣ה הַכֹּהֵן֒ וְהִנֵּה֙ לֹא־ פָשָׂ֣ה הַנֶּ֔גַע בַּבֶּ֕גֶד א֥וֹ בַשְּׁתִ֖י א֣וֹ בָעֵ֑רֶב א֖וֹ בְּכָל־ כְּלִי־ עֽוֹר׃ וְצִוָּה֙ הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וְכִ֨בְּס֔וּ אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־ בּ֖וֹ הַנָּ֑גַע וְהִסְגִּיר֥וֹ שִׁבְעַת־ יָמִ֖ים שֵׁנִֽית׃

passages.text: After it has been washed, the priest is to reexamine it, and if the mildewed article has not changed in appearance, it is unclean. Even though the mildew has not spread, you must burn it, whether the rot is on the front or back.
passages.sermon:
A priest examines the item after it is washed.
The item may be fabric, leather, woven, or knitted.
If the mildew has not changed in appearance, the item is still unclean.
If the mildew has not spread, the item is still unclean.
You must burn the item in the fire.
This rule applies whether the rot is on the front or the back of the item.
passages.original: וְרָאָ֨ה הַכֹּהֵ֜ן אַחֲרֵ֣י׀ הֻכַּבֵּ֣ס אֶת־ הַנֶּ֗גַע וְ֠הִנֵּה לֹֽא־ הָפַ֨ךְ הַנֶּ֤גַע אֶת־ עֵינוֹ֙ וְהַנֶּ֣גַע לֹֽא־ פָשָׂ֔ה טָמֵ֣א ה֔וּא בָּאֵ֖שׁ תִּשְׂרְפֶ֑נּוּ פְּחֶ֣תֶת הִ֔וא בְּקָרַחְתּ֖וֹ א֥וֹ בְגַבַּחְתּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: If the priest examines it and the mildew has faded after it has been washed, he must cut the contaminated section out of the fabric, leather, weave, or knit.
passages.sermon:
A priest examines the item.
The item may be fabric, leather, weave, or knit.
The item has a mildew spot.
Someone has already washed the item.
The priest sees that the mildew has faded.
The priest must cut out the contaminated section.
He removes the affected part from the fabric, leather, weave, or knit.
passages.original: וְאִם֮ רָאָ֣ה הַכֹּהֵן֒ וְהִנֵּה֙ כֵּהָ֣ה הַנֶּ֔גַע אַחֲרֵ֖י הֻכַּבֵּ֣ס אֹת֑וֹ וְקָרַ֣ע אֹת֗וֹ מִן־ הַבֶּ֙גֶד֙ א֣וֹ מִן־ הָע֔וֹר א֥וֹ מִן־ הַשְּׁתִ֖י א֥וֹ מִן־ הָעֵֽרֶב׃

passages.text: But if it reappears in the fabric, weave, or knit, or on any leather article, it is spreading. You must burn the contaminated article.
passages.sermon:
A priest examines the item for mildew.
The item can be fabric, weave, knit, or any leather article.
If the mildew appears again after washing, it is spreading.
The mildew is still present.
You must burn the item that has the mildew.
Burn the contaminated article in the fire.
passages.original: וְאִם־ תֵּרָאֶ֨ה ע֜וֹד בַּ֠בֶּגֶד אֽוֹ־ בַשְּׁתִ֤י אֽוֹ־ בָעֵ֙רֶב֙ א֣וֹ בְכָל־ כְּלִי־ ע֔וֹר פֹּרַ֖חַת הִ֑וא בָּאֵ֣שׁ תִּשְׂרְפֶ֔נּוּ אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־ בּ֖וֹ הַנָּֽגַע׃

passages.text: If the mildew disappears from the fabric, weave, or knit, or any leather article after washing, then it is to be washed again, and it will be clean.
passages.sermon:
A priest examines an item for mildew.
\r\nThe item can be fabric, weave, knit, or any leather article.
\r\nSomeone washes the item.
\r\nIf the mildew disappears after washing, the item must be washed again.
\r\nAfter the second washing, the item is clean.
passages.original: וְהַבֶּ֡גֶד אֽוֹ־ הַשְּׁתִ֨י אוֹ־ הָעֵ֜רֶב אֽוֹ־ כָל־ כְּלִ֤י הָעוֹר֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תְּכַבֵּ֔ס וְסָ֥ר מֵהֶ֖ם הַנָּ֑גַע וְכֻבַּ֥ס שֵׁנִ֖ית וְטָהֵֽר׃

passages.text: This is the law concerning a mildew contamination in wool or linen fabric, weave, or knit, or any leather article, for pronouncing it clean or unclean.”
passages.sermon:
God gave laws to Moses.
These laws concern mildew contamination.
Mildew can appear in wool fabric.
Mildew can appear in linen fabric.
Mildew can appear in woven material.
Mildew can appear in knitted material.
Mildew can appear in any leather article.
These laws tell how to decide if the item is clean.
These laws tell how to decide if the item is unclean.
passages.original: זֹ֠את תּוֹרַ֨ת נֶֽגַע־ צָרַ֜עַת בֶּ֥גֶד הַצֶּ֣מֶר׀ א֣וֹ הַפִּשְׁתִּ֗ים א֤וֹ הַשְּׁתִי֙ א֣וֹ הָעֵ֔רֶב א֖וֹ כָּל־ כְּלִי־ ע֑וֹר לְטַהֲר֖וֹ א֥וֹ לְטַמְּאֽוֹ׃פ
